Sam Most was born in Atlantic City on December 16, 1930. He was playing professionally by the age of 18, spending time in the sax sections of bands led by Tommy Dorsey, Boyd Raeburn and Don Redman. While equally accomplished on tenor sax and clarinet, it is Sam’s flute playing that is recognized as a major contribution to jazz. Since the early 1950s, Sam has been pioneering on the flute, developing new techniques and influencing future jazz artists. He has traveled extensively and performed with a long list of fellow jazz greats, including Buddy Rich, Henry Mancini, Gerry Mulligan and Art Blakey.
Sam currently performs in the Los Angeles area and can occasionally be found on the bandstand with his brother, clarinetist Abe Most.
Sam was interviewed in Los Angeles on February 15, 1999, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.

My name is Monk Rowe and we are in Los Angeles filming for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive. I’ve been looking forward to talking with Sam Most, saxophonist, flautist and clarinetist. You’ve been around for a long time, like on the forefront of a number of things in jazz. So welcome.
